title: Governance Playbook for Design System Contributions, RFCs, and Deprecation
creator: Anya Patel
description: Create a single, actionable governance playbook for the design system that covers: contribution guidelines (how to propose/ship new tokens and components), the RFC process for non-trivial changes, a lightweight review checklist for designers and engineers, and a clear deprecation policy for components and tokens. The goal is to reduce friction for contributors while protecting product stability and accessibility across Redwood products.
acceptance_criteria: One-page contribution checklist that fits in a PR description
RFC template added to the design repo and referenced in the playbook
Deprecation policy with timelines: announcement -> soft-deprecation -> removal
Migration guide template for deprecated components/tokens
Signoff flow documented with at least two designated approvers (Design steward + Component owner)
Design Console (docs site) has a Governance section linking the playbook, RFCs, and open deprecations
checklist: Draft playbook: contribution steps, code and design artifact requirements
Define roles: Design steward, Component owner, Release owner, Eng reviewer
Create RFC template: problem, alternatives, impact, rollout plan, metrics
Build a deprecation timeline and notification cadence (email/changelog/docs)
Add accessibility and localization checks to review checklist
Publish playbook to docs and add link to starter PR template
Run a pilot with two incoming component PRs and iterate based on feedback
deprecation_policy_summary: Deprecation is a three-stage process: 1) Announcement — public notice + migration notes (30 days), 2) Soft-deprecation — mark in docs and console; warn in PR checks and logs (90 days), 3) Removal — component/code gets removed from main branch and runtime (after migration window, default 180 days). Exceptions may be made for critical security fixes or compliance needs with faster timelines.
migration_requirements: Provide example migration code snippets (JS/TS/React) and token mapping table
Include visual diffs and QA checklist for designers
Automated codemod or eslint rule suggested when possible
Customer-impact assessment and list of known internal consumers
review_process: Contributions follow: 1) Submit PR with design artifacts (Figma link), accessibility notes, and unit/visual tests. 2) Request review from Component owner and cross-team Eng reviewer. 3) Design steward gives final design acceptance. For RFCs, circulate to Design + Eng + PM for 7 business days, collect decisions, and publish outcome. Emergency changes require a documented rollback plan and at least one engineering lead approval.
stakeholders: Component Owners: (listed per component in CODEOWNERS)
Engineering Reviewers: Runtime and Console teams
Product Managers: release and customer-impact review
Docs/Developer Experience: publish and maintain guidance
